source_title: 2 killed as building collapses in Delhi, bodies recovered after overnight rescue ops - India Today
source_excerpt:
The incident comes a month after a five-storey building housing a student hostel collapsed in south Delhi's Satya Niketan area on September 6, killing seven people and injuring several others.
Two men were killed after a building structure collapsed in northeast Delhi’s Harsh Vihar area on Sunday evening. The victims, identified as Chanderpal (60) and his son Vijay Kumar (33), were rescued from the debris during an overnight operation and taken to GTB Hospital this morning, where doctors declared them dead.
The incident comes weeks after a five-storey building housing a student hostel collapsed in south Delhi’s Satya Niketan area on September 6 , killing seven people and injuring several others. On October 6, another building in northeast Delhi’s Seemapuri area collapsed, killing three people, including a child .
According to the police, information about the collapse at A-4, Milan Garden in Harsh Vihar, was received at 6.46 pm on Sunday. A police team promptly reached the spot and joined the rescue efforts. OLD BUILDING WITH GODOWN ON GROUND FLOOR COLLAPSES
OLD BUILDING WITH GODOWN ON GROUND FLOOR COLLAPSES
A preliminary inspection revealed that the ground-floor structure of an old building, which reportedly housed a godown, collapsed along with the first-floor structure built above it. The property is reportedly owned by Manoj Kumar, according to the police.
Two fire brigade vehicles, two ambulances and a crane were deployed at the site. Civil Defence volunteers and teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Delhi Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) and Delhi Fire Service also joined the overnight rescue operation.
According to news agency PTI, the two bodies were recovered from the rubble on Monday morning following the overnight rescue operation. The deceased were residents of Harsh Vihar.
The police said legal action was being initiated under relevant provisions of law, while further investigation into the incident was underway. KAPIL MISHRA LINKS COLLAPSE TO ILLEGAL CONSTRUCTION
KAPIL MISHRA LINKS COLLAPSE TO ILLEGAL CONSTRUCTION
After the collapse, Delhi Ministers Kapil Mishra and Ashish Sood reached the site to assess the situation.
Mishra said an attempt to install a new lintel appeared to have triggered the collapse, causing the floor below to cave in as well. The two victims were reportedly a father and son.
He said the circumstances surrounding the collapse would be investigated and linked such incidents to illegal construction, referring to previous building collapses in Seemapuri, Seelampur, Mustafabad and Babarpur.
“The reasons behind the collapses in Seemapuri, Seelampur, Mustafabad, and Babarpur are well-known, and the sites have been inspected. We visited those locations as well, and it is clear that such incidents are a direct consequence of illegal construction,” he told ANI.
The investigation into the Harsh Vihar collapse is underway, with police initiating legal action under the relevant provisions of law. - Ends
